_provenance: Error-string SHAPES reproduced from advisors/composer_backtest_client.py's own f-string templates (read directly from source, never invented). A genuine live infra outage (connection refused / DNS failure / 5xx / 429-exhausted) cannot be safely or ethically captured against the real Composer API, and doing so would violate the project's 'never hit live Composer in tests' rule -- so these are FORMAT fixtures (the literal template each failure branch emits), not live-captured payloads, matching the same discipline as the existing _envelope() helper in tests/advisors/test_plan_tree_compiler_repair.py.

http_5xx_exhausted.source: advisors/composer_backtest_client.py:360 -- f"HTTP {response.status_code}: {response.text[:200]}" (reached when a retryable 5xx status has exhausted max_retries)

http_429_rate_limit_exhausted.source: advisors/composer_backtest_client.py:332 -- f"HTTP 429 rate limit exceeded; Retry-After={retry_after:.0f}s" (reached when 429 retries are exhausted)
http_429_rate_limit_exhausted.note: Does NOT match the compiler's '^HTTP (\d+):' envelope-status regex (no colon after the digits) -- classifies as non-parseable, not as a parsed status=429.

timeout.example: request timed out after 120s: HTTPSConnectionPool timeout

transport_error.example: transport error: ConnectionError: Failed to establish a new connection

invalid_json_200.example: invalid JSON in 200 response: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
invalid_json_200.note: Composer responded 200 but the body was not parseable JSON -- not a genuine data reject, structurally identical (non-parseable-by-status) to the other infra shapes.
